    #84914. Latest Update: Kushner-backed OakNorth secures U.S. bank charter as global digital banks push into America

    📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (633 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Latest Update: Kushner-backed OakNorth secures U.S. bank charter as global digital banks push into America

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (633 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The U.K.'s OakNorth has secured a federal bank charter, saying it is the first foreign digital bank to do so, as international competitors vie for U.S.
    • The charter clears OakNorth, which is backed by Jared Kushner's private equity firm, to acquire Michigan-based Community Unity Bank, subject to an $80 million capital injection, according to approval documents issued by the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency on Nov.
    • The deal, which is expected to close by the end of 2026, would allow OakNorth to provide loans, take deposits, and offer other banking services across all 50 states.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The U.K.'s OakNorth has secured a federal bank charter, saying it is the first foreign digital bank to do so, as international competitors vie for U.S. market share.

    The charter clears OakNorth, which is backed by Jared Kushner's private equity firm, to acquire Michigan-based Community Unity Bank, subject to an $80 million capital injection, according to approval documents issued by the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency on Nov. 19.

    The deal, which is expected to close by the end of 2026, would allow OakNorth to provide loans, take deposits, and offer other banking services across all 50 states.

    Kushner's private equity firm, Affinity Partners, took an 8% stake in OakNorth in 2025, with backing from major Gulf investors, including the sovereign wealth funds of Saudi Arabia and Qatar. SoftBank is also an OakNorth investor.

    The bank reported $295 million in pretax profit for 2025 in its annual report, up from $280 million the previous year and close to three times the $100 million in profits five years prior.

    It stated principal losses on $20 billion in credit facilities issued over the past 10 years totaled £9 million, or less than 0.05%. Its 1.4% return on assets placed it among the top five banks in Western Europe and in the top 1% of commercial banks globally, according to The Banker's rankings.

    "I would say that the level of animal spirits in the U.S. is always higher, right? So the momentum of business and the optimism is always a step up," OakNorth CEO Rishi Khosla told CNBC's "Squawk Box Europe" on Monday.

    He said U.S. economic growth, investment in artificial intelligence and infrastructure spending would create opportunities for the bank.

    Recent findings suggest that oakNorth has focused on lending to lower mid-market businesses rather than competing for consumer customers in a crowded U.S. market.

    It has been revealed that the lender targets businesses with annual revenues of $5 million to $100 million with loans worth $5 million to $50 million. The bank entered the U.S. market in 2023 and has lent about $3.5 billion to U.S. businesses to date. The U.S. accounted for 40% of its $12.4 billion in upcoming loans in 2025.

    "These are really growth companies which are scaling up, and given that focus, you really haven't had an institution in the last decades that focus on that customer segment, and that's opened up the opportunity for us," Khosla noted.

    He cited commercial real estate lending as a particularly strong growth opportunity in the U.S.

    According to recent reports, securing the charter is notoriously difficult, with many regulatory hurdles. It took OakNorth 20 months, a restructure of the bank's corporate ownership, and relocating its holding organization from the island of Jersey to the U.K. to meet Federal Reserve requirements.

    In a recent development, other international fintechs seeking a foothold in the U.S. have struggled to gain traction. Monzo and Revolut withdrew their initial U.S. applications for a full banking charter between 2021 and 2023 after regulatory pushback.

    Recent findings suggest that monzo closed its U.S. operations in April just four years after it launched, amid a crowded consumer market. "We have made a strategic decision to focus on scaling in our home market and Europe and to step away from the U.S.," the organization said.

    But the regulatory landscape has since shifted. Revolut and Brazil's Nubank have received conditional approval for U.S. banking charters from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency.

    Dutch digital bank Bunq reapplied after withdrawing its 2023 application, but its second application was denied in August.

    According to recent reports, another U.K. digital lender, Starling, is also seeking U.S. growth. It sells its Engine banking software to mid-tier U.S. lenders and is looking to acquire a domestic bank to serve business clients.

    #84911. Six key questions raised by Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia

    📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1101 w)
    📖 Baca
    Hardware & Chips ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Six key questions raised by Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1101 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Jensen Huang made a dramatic return as Nvidia CEO on Monday, less than a week after board Chairman Harvey Jones noted directors did not intend to reinstate him.
    • Nvidia shares surged as much as 36% during the session and closed 31% higher.
    • It has been revealed that the reversal followed a steep decline in Nvidia shares, which closed at $125.53 on Friday even after the manufacturer reported strong third-quarter results.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Jensen Huang made a dramatic return as Nvidia CEO on Monday, less than a week after board Chairman Harvey Jones noted directors did not intend to reinstate him. The board later voted unanimously to bring Huang back.

    Nvidia shares surged as much as 36% during the session and closed 31% higher.

    It has been revealed that the reversal followed a steep decline in Nvidia shares, which closed at $125.53 on Friday even after the manufacturer reported strong third-quarter results. A petition calling for Huang's return had drawn more than 200,000 signatures, according to its organizers.

    The rally spread across the broader market, with the Nasdaq Composite gaining 6.5% and the S&P 500 rising 4.7%, each posting its strongest session since April 2025.

    Nvidia's board said it had received input from senior U.S. government officials and that its investigation into Huang's conduct would continue.

    Still, the board's reversal, President Donald Trump's administration's role and continued scrutiny of Nvidia's China business leave major questions for both investors and lawmakers.

    Industry observers note that sen. Jack Reed, a member of the Senate Banking Committee, urged Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick on Monday to appear before the committee to discuss the case.

    Reed did not lay out a specific list of questions for the two officials, but his statement cited reporting that Trump had been briefed by intelligence officials led by then-National Security Adviser Marco Rubio before intervening in support of Huang's return.

    Reed's call adds to mounting pressure on both Nvidia and the Trump administration to explain what they knew and when.

    Rep. Gabe Amo, D-R.I., vice ranking member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, said Huang’s reinstatement could broaden congressional scrutiny rather than bring it to a close.

    “I think it frankly broadens the scope of the query,” Amo told CNBC, adding that lawmakers should also examine administration officials involved in decisions affecting Nvidia and chip sales to China.

    Amo said he expects the planned closed-door interview with Huang on Dec. 1 to proceed and that Congress would continue seeking answers both privately and publicly in the coming months.

    According to recent reports, “He should start purchasing his plane tickets to Washington,” he said. “It is abundantly clear that this is ripe for questioning by Congress.”.

    In a recent development, on Nvidia's third-quarter earnings call on Nov. 17, Jones stated the board had accepted Huang's resignation and did not intend to reinstate him.

    Recent findings suggest that less than a week later, the board reversed course, saying Monday that it had unanimously voted to bring Huang back after discussions with him and input from senior U.S. government officials.

    Trump remarked he had spoken with board members and that his administration provided assurances based on the information available to it. But the board has not publicly detailed what it was told.

    "The board decided to do what we wanted to do," Trump told CNBC, adding that he believed his intervention had been important.

    "I've been speaking to the board directly and indirectly, and I felt very strongly about it," he said.

    Trump also called into an Nvidia board meeting to argue for Huang's return, Semafor reported, citing people familiar with the matter.

    Reed has called on Huang to disclose his communications with Trump and on Nvidia to release a transcript of the board's call with the president.

    Lawmakers are still seeking answers about the alleged smuggling of Nvidia products to China, their possible diversion for military use and possible advancement of Chinese AI capabilities.

    The Senate Banking Committee has scheduled Huang to testify on U.S. export controls on Dec. 3. House lawmakers have also confirmed closed-door interviews with Huang on Dec. 1 and Nvidia General Counsel Tim Teter on Dec. 2.

    According to recent reports, "The Nvidia board's brief internal investigation and reinstatement of Jensen Huang do not erase the national security threats and questions that must be addressed," Reps. John Moolenaar, Rick Crawford and Brian Mast said in a joint statement.

    Their inquiry may also examine what Nvidia knew about the customers and resellers involved, as well as what controls the tech giant had in place.

    According to recent reports, other lawmakers have also sought to preserve the paper trail. Sens. Elizabeth Warren and Chris Coons had asked senior administration officials on Nov. 11 to retain records related to Nvidia exports of advanced AI chips to China and associated national security concerns.

    According to recent reports, nvidia has promised to hire a chief compliance officer and establish a committee overseeing national security and export controls. The board's investigation into Huang's conduct also remains underway.

    Josh Gilbert, eToro's lead analyst for APAC and the Middle East, mentioned investors will be watching whether those latest safeguards carry meaningful authority.

    Succession remains another question.

    Gil Luria, head of technology research at D.A. Davidson, mentioned Nvidia has a limited window to prepare for the possibility that a future president may be less supportive of Huang.

    With Trump's term ending in two years, Luria argued that Nvidia needs a clearer plan for who could take over if Huang were forced to leave again.

    Sources indicate that gilbert pointed to Nvidia's roughly 75% revenue-growth forecast for the next financial year as evidence of strong near-term demand. The longer-term question, he said, is whether customer orders and artificial intelligence investment can sustain that pace.

    Luria told CNBC that concerns about the broader AI trade remain, including the cost of financing data centers, potential overbuilding by neocloud companies and obstacles to building new facilities.

    It has been revealed that bernstein analyst Stacy Rasgon remarked worries about whether AI spending is achievable and sustainable were not caused solely by Huang's departure. UBS, meanwhile, flagged Nvidia's roughly $390 billion in supply commitments and the need to keep demand flowing through its ecosystem.

    According to recent reports, gilbert said part of Monday's rally reflected investors recovering earlier losses rather than pricing in new growth. Bernstein restored its "Outperform" rating and kept its $200 price target, while UBS maintained its $220 target.

    "For the share price, it comes down to whether Nvidia can keep delivering as it has done over recent years," stated Gilbert, adding that Huang's return could ease some concerns about Nvidia's longer-term outlook.

    Sources indicate that "The real worry has been what happens beyond next year. Having Huang back at the helm goes a long way to easing those concerns, because he's the one who sits down with the biggest customers and gets those multi-year orders over the line," he said.

    — CNBC's David Sucherman, Justin Papp and Eko Prasetyo contributed to the story.

    #84909. Op-ed: Trump’s Nvidia board intervention put a price on national security. Our adversaries will take note

    📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1658 w)
    📖 Baca
    Hardware & Chips ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Op-ed: Trump’s Nvidia board intervention put a price on national security. Our adversaries will take note

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1658 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that president Donald J.
    • In a recent development, on Monday, after Nvidia's board reinstated Huang following his resignation amid a counterintelligence controversy and allegations that Alice Huang, with whom he had an affair, is under suspicion of being a Chinese intelligence asset, Wall Street celebrated with a historic market bounce.
    • What happened at Nvidia raises the frightening possibility that it does, and it fits a recent pattern that is exactly what geopolitical rivals around the world want to see.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that president Donald J. Trump has accomplished something extraordinary. He directly inserted himself into the boardroom of one of America's most strategically notable companies, Nvidia, helping to reverse a corporate leadership decision, and personally vouched for restored CEO Jensen Huang as having a clean bill of health regarding the national security investigations into his business activities with China.

    In a recent development, on Monday, after Nvidia's board reinstated Huang following his resignation amid a counterintelligence controversy and allegations that Alice Huang, with whom he had an affair, is under suspicion of being a Chinese intelligence asset, Wall Street celebrated with a historic market bounce. But the market's enthusiasm should not obscure a far more consequential question circulating in Washington, D.C.: Does American national security have a price?

    What happened at Nvidia raises the frightening possibility that it does, and it fits a recent pattern that is exactly what geopolitical rivals around the world want to see. Consider the economic pressures surrounding the Iran war. Disruptions to energy markets, shipping, supply chains, and consumer prices have complicated American strategic decision-making. These are notably different circumstances, but they raise the same troubling question about the costs of defending American national security interests, and when they become economically unpalatable to those in the Trump administration.

    Beijing, Tehran, and Moscow are watching — as are our allies and partners — and they all may agree on one thing: America has an Achilles' heel that military and technological superiority cannot overcome. It is possible to impose sufficient economic pain to alter Washington's strategic calculation with friends and foes alike. Bleed American capital markets, disrupt commerce, squeeze consumers, and eventually Washington may look for an exit.

    Despite the narrative that the president is weaving, there is a fundamental difference between responsibly weighing economic consequences and allowing adversaries to conclude that they can impose an economic veto over U.S. national security policy. Trump told CNBC in an extensive interview on Monday morning that when it comes to national security, "losing the brain power of somebody like Jensen ... would be a far bigger threat than anything we're talking about.".

    It has been revealed that "The bigger impact was the long term. The bigger impact was you know he's got other chips in his brain that nobody else knows about, including me, that nobody else understands," Trump noted. "This was a big loss. This was a tremendous loss. And you saw that it affected the market. It affected even, I think it even affected the perception of our country in the world," the president said.

    And that's true, but not only in the way Trump thinks it did.

    This is not about whether Huang is a brilliant executive or whether Nvidia is enormously important to American competitiveness. Both are true. The question that America, particularly its government, must ask is whether Huang's economic importance justifies subordinating corporate governance, interfering with counterintelligence procedures, and stymying national security oversight.

    Trump characterized the Justice Department's assessment as having exonerated Huang. Yet Nvidia's board reinstated him while its own review remained open.

    The allegations involving reported contacts with Chinese intelligence assets do not establish legal wrongdoing. However, presidential personal assurances are not substitutes for independent counterintelligence assessments and investigations or congressional oversight. Monday's rising stock price might only measure what shareholders believe Huang at the helm of Nvidia is worth, while discounting or ignoring the unresolved counterintelligence risk that he may still pose to Nvidia and the entire artificial intelligence ecosystem.

    The Trump administration, Silicon Valley, and Wall Street may believe the matter is closed.

    "That thing's like a rocket ship going in the wrong direction. Now it's a rocket ship going in the right direction, and it's taking the whole market," Trump told CNBC about Nvidia's 31.5% Monday gains.

    One glaring vulnerability still on the horizon is what Washington does not know. If Beijing possesses additional damaging information, it controls whether, when, and how that information might be weaponized in an ongoing and now reignited strategic competition between the U.S. and China. Beijing retains the capacity to reopen this matter at a time of its choosing. Chinese intelligence could drip-feed disclosures, compel repeated explanations from Huang and the president, and transform Monday's declaration of resolution of this matter into a prolonged national security vulnerability.

    It has been revealed that there is also a striking irony here. Some pundits are comparing Trump's intervention to China's state-controlled market. To be sure, the Chinese government has a very heavy hand in its economy, but one thing the Chinese Communist Party will never do is put an individual ahead of national security and political authority despite the economic impact that this person or firm is perceived to have. Xi Jinping and China's Communist Party have demonstrated a willingness to make almost the opposite calculation about national security and economic growth. Under Xi, national and political security generally takes precedence over the interests of individual companies and brilliant executives.

    Consider Jack Ma. In 2020, Beijing halted Ant Group's planned $37 billion initial public offering and subsequently imposed sweeping regulatory restrictions on Ma's business empire. Beijing accepted substantial economic consequences to reinforce national security and political authority. This is not an argument for importing China's authoritarian model into American corporate governance. But the strategic asymmetry is noteworthy to revisit in this latest comparative context. Beijing has demonstrated that even its most celebrated entrepreneurs are not indispensable to the party and the nation. Washington risks signaling that some of its entrepreneurs are in fact indispensable to the state, which ironically potentially makes them even bigger intelligence targets for foreign adversaries.

    As an economic matter, the commercial realities of Nvidia's China business make this situation even more perplexing. China, including Hong Kong, accounted for just 9.1% of Nvidia's reported global revenue in fiscal 2026, down from 19.2% the previous year. Its latest fourth-quarter guidance assumes no Chinese data center compute revenue. Nvidia did change the way it reports geographic sales, to customer headquarter address, in late 2025. But anyone familiar with Chinese strategic documents, including the 15th Five-Year Plan, should understand that Beijing has no intention of becoming permanently "addicted" to American chips. Its objective is technological self-reliance, not expanding Nvidia's market share and by extension its dependency on them.

    Recent findings suggest that whatever the exact figure, I cannot think of a number that is worth selling out U.S. national security over, but it certainly isn't  9.1%, which is also a number that will continue to shrink. Furthermore, if the AI ecosystem is critical to our economy and our national security, then selling advanced chips to China or loosening export controls is the opposite of what we should be doing because the chips are used to juice the compute of Chinese LLMs that compete with ours, and to increase the effectiveness and lethality of Chinese weapons systems. The questionable sales of Nvidia chips in Asia, which are at the heart of this story, support neither our economy nor our national security. They undermine them both.

    Recent findings suggest that there is also an extraordinary corporate governance precedent that extends well beyond Nvidia and Huang, one that is escalating and growing more bold at each turn. While Trump has intervened in the markets before, in cases including U.S. Steel and Intel, he has never gone to this level, making the argument that a organization is so critical to the national security of the nation that at any point its decision making could require executive branch intervention and specific direction.

    Recent findings suggest that based on the president's rationale, what should the boards of key national security relevant companies like Boeing, Lockheed Martin, Palantir, Anduril, SpaceX, or even Rio Tinto — whose jointly owned Resolution Copper project in Arizona could eventually supply up to 25 percent of America's copper demand — expect? Does their strategic importance justify presidential intervention in executive appointments, succession planning, corporate strategy, or commercial relationships? A precedent established by one president becomes an idea, option, and instrument available to future presidents, including those with fundamentally different political preferences.

    Recent findings suggest that all of this brings us to Congress. If you take Trump at his word, that Nvidia's strategic importance justifies extraordinary executive branch intervention, it also justifies extraordinary legislative intervention and oversight. Article I grants Congress authority to regulate foreign commerce. Congress established the statutory framework governing executive export-control authority through legislation, including the Export Control Reform Act of 2018. Those authorities were delegated, not surrendered. The president may have driven this Nvidia CEO decision by telephone. Congress possesses something more enduring: the authority to establish the rules through legislation. The Senate Banking Committee's scheduled December 3 hearing on export controls provides an opportunity to begin.

    Congress should do much more than demand classified briefings on the counterintelligence concerns. Lawmakers should pass, with veto-proof majorities, requirements for stronger board-level counterintelligence responsibilities, mandatory defensive briefings to vulnerable tech executives and innovation sector leadership, much tighter export-license oversight with enforcement mechanisms that have teeth, and enforceable reporting requirements. Legislative proposals including the AI Overwatch Act, Match Act, and Remote Access Security Act must be passed as soon as possible. Nvidia and its leadership may warrant considerably tighter legal and regulatory scrutiny given its importance as the fulcrum of the AI ecosystem.

    In a recent development, it is important for Congress to remember that the legislative branch is a co-equal branch of government, not a rubber stamp or talk shop providing us with commentary about the outcome of executive branch decisions. They have an active and constitutional role to play in our democracy. They need to get it together and get to work. If Nvidia is important enough for the president to enter its boardroom, it is important enough for Congress to exercise its constitutional authority over the rules governing this entire process.

    —By Dewardic McNeal, Managing Director and Senior Policy Analyst at Longview Global, and a CNBC Contributor.

    #84907. Tech Report: Nvidia has lost $2 trillion in value. Here's what options traders expect from earnings

    📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (522 w)
    📖 Baca
    Hardware & Chips ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Tech Report: Nvidia has lost $2 trillion in value. Here's what options traders expect from earnings

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (522 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Jensen Huang's forced exit from Nvidia shocked Wall Street and Washington, wiped $2 trillion off its market value, and raised serious questions about national security and regulation of the AI complex.
    • With volatility in the stock near the highest since April 2025, options traders are now pricing a 7% reaction in the stock after its report, the biggest implied move going into an Nvidia report since February 2025, and well above the median move of 3.2% over the last eight quarters.
    • Recent findings suggest that implied volatility reached 68 Monday, compared to under 40 in early October, according to ThinkOrSwim data.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Jensen Huang's forced exit from Nvidia shocked Wall Street and Washington, wiped $2 trillion off its market value, and raised serious questions about national security and regulation of the AI complex. Traders, for the moment, must content themselves with the comparatively mundane business of Tuesday's earnings, and options traders are expecting big moves.

    With volatility in the stock near the highest since April 2025, options traders are now pricing a 7% reaction in the stock after its report, the biggest implied move going into an Nvidia report since February 2025, and well above the median move of 3.2% over the last eight quarters.

    Recent findings suggest that implied volatility reached 68 Monday, compared to under 40 in early October, according to ThinkOrSwim data. Nvidia vol reached a multi-year high above 92 in the aftermath of President Trump's tariff Liberation day in April '25. In other words, the tech giant that for much of the AI boom was the most reliable winner in the market, is now more volatile than all but 35 companies in the S&P 500.

    "Longer term, I see significant downside risk unless Nvidia can attract an exceptional leader, someone like Tim Cook or AMD's Lisa Su," Nigam Arora, founder of the Arora report, noted in a text ahead of the company's after-market report on Tuesday.

    Recent findings suggest that since hitting all-time highs in October, Nvidia shares have fallen 35%, shedding $2 trillion in market capitalization along the way. Including Nvidia, there are only five companies in the S&P 500 worth more than $2 trillion. However, there is evidence that bulls have been holding out hope while bears snatch up profits: the ratio of open puts to call contracts has actually widened towards calls, according to Barchart data. The ratio is right now 0.87, down from a one-year high of 1.02 two weeks ago and the lowest since the first week of October.

    The most popular contract by volume on Monday was the 155-strike put expiring at the bell Monday, but the most popular trade for later expiry was the 160-strike call expiring Thursday, and the second-most-common purchase was the 190-strike call expiring Friday, SpotGamma data show.

    According to recent reports, one catch is that most call contracts traded Monday looked like neutral to bearish positions opened by traders selling calls. Of the 5 million options traded on Monday, 3 million were calls, but more were likely opened by sellers than buyers. Of the $2.3 billion in options premium traded on Nvidia Monday, $1.2 billion was tied to puts, SpotGamma data show.

    It has been revealed that with bears taking profits in puts the past month, there's another potential snag on open interest. There are very few open put contracts at or below the $157 level at which the stock closed Monday. That suggests any bad surprise would find many traders with little downside protection.

    By the same token, there's notable open interest in call contracts from the 175-strike and above, suggesting profit-taking on a bounce could limit Nvidia's recovery past levels it breached over the past week.

    Either way, Tuesday's earnings could provide fireworks.

    #84904. Latest Update: AG Blanche, FBI’s Patel dodge questions about Jensen Huang investigation

    📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (514 w)
    📖 Baca
    Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Latest Update: AG Blanche, FBI’s Patel dodge questions about Jensen Huang investigation

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (514 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Attorney General Todd Blanche and FBI Director Kash Patel on Tuesday dodged questions about the conclusions of an investigation President Donald Trump cited to push Nvidia's board to bring back Jensen Huang as CEO.
    • Asked by a reporter whether the Department of Justice had investigated Huang and the results of that probe, Blanche said, "What the president said is that he talked to a lot of people going into the decision that he made to encourage the board to reinstate him.".
    • "And so I'm not going to get into communications I have with the president," Blanche stated at a news conference in Washington.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Attorney General Todd Blanche and FBI Director Kash Patel on Tuesday dodged questions about the conclusions of an investigation President Donald Trump cited to push Nvidia's board to bring back Jensen Huang as CEO.

    Asked by a reporter whether the Department of Justice had investigated Huang and the results of that probe, Blanche said, "What the president said is that he talked to a lot of people going into the decision that he made to encourage the board to reinstate him.".

    "And so I'm not going to get into communications I have with the president," Blanche stated at a news conference in Washington.

    Huang was reinstated as CEO of Nvidia on Monday morning, less than two weeks after resigning amid allegations he had affairs with a purported spy for China and two Nvidia employees plus concerns that advanced semiconductor chips made by his organization had been diverted to China in violation of U.S. law.

    In an interview with CNBC on Monday, Trump was asked what led him to personally confirm to Nvidia's board that Huang was not a national security risk.

    "We've done a very thorough investigation, and the investigation showed that he did, I mean, he had bad judgment having to do with somewhat unrelated incidents, but he did nothing wrong," Trump replied.

    According to recent reports, trump in a Truth Social post on Monday remarked the U.S. government had no reason to believe Huang's return to the firm "poses any risk to National Security," and that Blanche had confirmed the government "does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct.".

    It has been revealed that nvidia, in its statement Monday announcing Huang's return, said, "The Board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang's reinstatement poses no national security risk.".

    Blanche on Tuesday mentioned, "Nvidia is a good corporate citizen.".

    "Obviously, if Nvidia was the target, or was the subject of some criminal investigation, or they were obstructing or thwarting our investigation, then that wouldn't be the message that the president is saying to the American people," he said.

    Patel did not answer a reporter's question of whether the FBI has spoken to Huang and whether the FBI had been made aware of an assessment by U.S. intelligence agencies that Huang's reported paramour, Alice Huang, was an asset for China's spy agency.

    Jensen Huang is not related to Alice Huang, who was an executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based customer of Nvidia's semiconductor chips.

    In a recent development, the DOJ and Commerce Department on Nov. 17 said they were investigating Megaspeed for potential diversion of Nvidia chips in violation of U.S. export law.

    Asked how the DOJ could rule out Jensen Huang having potential criminal liability given the fact that the investigation remains ongoing, Blanche replied, "So, when you say the export investigation is still ongoing, I don't know what you're talking about.".

    "We have hundreds, if not more, export investigations going at any time at the Department of Justice," Blanche said.

    #84903. Karl-Anthony Towns for MVP? Knicks star is making case as the best player in the East

    📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 12m • 📚 Deep Dive (2487 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Yahoo ↗ Open Full Page

    Karl-Anthony Towns for MVP? Knicks star is making case as the best player in the East

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 12 min read (2487 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Yahoo

    ⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that it's not the point of the video, I know.
    • Recent findings suggest that what you see at the start of the video, though, is a sign posted inside the Knicks' locker room highlighting the principles that head coach Mike Brown has identified as the non-negotiable foundations of Upcoming York's offense: pace, space, quick decisions, paint touches, crash the glass.
    • That's kind of perfect, because nobody's exemplifying those principles better right now than the Knicks' All-Star center … and, when you really take a look at it, very, very few people in the NBA can credibly claim to be playing any better than him.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that it's not the point of the video, I know. The clip the Upcoming York Knicks posted late Sunday night was intended to celebrate Josh Hart producing arguably his best performance in what's been a rocky start to the season — 10 points, 11 rebounds, 10 assists and a steal, his 18th triple-double in a Knicks uniform, tied for the second-most in franchise history — in a 113-106 win over the rival Indiana Pacers at Madison Square Garden.

    Recent findings suggest that what you see at the start of the video, though, is a sign posted inside the Knicks' locker room highlighting the principles that head coach Mike Brown has identified as the non-negotiable foundations of Upcoming York's offense: pace, space, quick decisions, paint touches, crash the glass. And at the very start of the clip, before the camera pans over to Hart, there's only one Knicks player in sight: Karl-Anthony Towns.

    That's kind of perfect, because nobody's exemplifying those principles better right now than the Knicks' All-Star center … and, when you really take a look at it, very, very few people in the NBA can credibly claim to be playing any better than him.

    The early-season MVP conversation pretty much starts and ends with Victor Wembanyama and Luka Dončić, the scoreboard-breaking titans leading the top two squads in the Western Conference. Expand the parameters out a little bit, though, and Towns — whose contract Knicks owner James L. Dolan declined to extend before the start of the season, and man, does it sure seem like the price is going up with every passing game — is forcing his way into the tier below them.

    The Knicks are, and always will be, Jalen Brunson's team. Through the first month of the 2026-27 NBA season, though — and, really, since the start of last postseason — you can make a legitimate case that Towns has been their best all-around player. And, if you're feeling spicy, maybe the best player in the entire conference.

    Recent findings suggest that that's debatable, of course. Reasonable people can forward a number of names: Giannis Antetokounmpo, off to a scorching start to his tenure in South Beach; Cade Cunningham, still the straw that stirs the drink in Detroit; Tyrese Maxey, who's been the best player on the conference's No. 1 seed in Philly; Jayson Tatum, who had Boston off to a roaring start before some slippage out West.

    Dig into the numbers, though, and Towns — the two-way heartbeat of a team that has won 11 of its past 14 games since an 0-3 start to move into a tie for second place in the East, boasting the NBA's third-best net rating in that span — has as good a case as any of them.

    Entering Tuesday's action, Towns ranks third in the NBA in ESPN's net points per 100 possessions, behind only Wembanyama and Dončić. He's fourth in win shares, behind only Wembanyama, Dončić and Houston Rockets center Alperen Şengün. He's fifth in The BBall Index's LEBRON and box plus-minus, and sixth in win shares per 48 minutes, value over replacement player, Neil Paine's wins above replacement and Mike Beuoy's win probability added. He's seventh in player efficiency rating, ninth in DARKO daily plus-minus and tied for 10th among healthy players in Jeremias Engelmann's xRAPM. Which is to say: Take your pick of impact metrics, and KAT's right near the top, rubbing shoulders with the best of the best.

    Maybe you're not such a big fan of the all-in-one alphabet-soup metrics; maybe you like your numbers a little less advanced. Well, how's this:.

    Towns enters Wednesday's 2026 Emirates NBA Cup meeting with the rival Cleveland Cavaliers averaging 21.8 points, 13.9 rebounds and 4.0 assists in 32.6 minutes per game. That makes him one of only three players in the NBA this season averaging at least 20 points, 10 rebounds and four dimes a night, alongside Antetokounmpo and Nikola Jokić. He's hitting those numbers more efficiently than ever, too, shooting 61% on 2-pointers and 42% from long distance, scoring under 1.32 points per shot attempt with a .650 true shooting percentage (which factors in 2-point, 3-point and free-throw accuracy) — both career highs.

    (Bruno Rouby/Yahoo Sports Illustration).

    Scoring plus rebounding plus playmaking plus efficiency is a pretty damn good combination. Prior to this season, Stathead's database lists only two players who've ever averaged more than 20 points per game, grabbed more than 20% of available rebounds, dished assists on more than 20% of his teammates' baskets, and posted a true shooting percentage north of .600: Giannis, back in 2019-20, and Jokić, who did it in 2021-22, '22-23 and '25-26.

    Those seasons resulted in two MVP trophies and two runner-up finishes. That's the organization that KAT's keeping this season.

    (For the record: Wemby and Giannis are also keeping that firm this season. Whew.).

    Much of this stellar start goes back to those five principles — pace, space, quick decisions, paint touches, crash the glass — that Brown's been hammering ever since he got to Latest York. Towns might not be the first person you think of when you hear the word "pace," and the Knicks probably wouldn't be the first team to come to mind: They rank dead last in the NBA in number of possessions per 48 minutes, and tied for 28th in the average length of their offensive possessions. (Much, at times, to Brown's chagrin.) But while nobody will confuse Brown's charges for the Seven Seconds or Less Suns, they do move more swiftly with the 7-footer involved: The Knicks' average offensive possession is 1.3 seconds faster with Towns on the floor than off it — the largest differential of any Knick who's played actual minutes.

    Industry observers note that "Space," obviously, is a little easier to square here. Long heralded as perhaps the sweetest-shooting big man of all time (including, um, by himself), Towns is attempting eight 3-pointers per 100 possessions this season, the most since his last season in Minnesota and the fourth-most of his career. He boasts the third-highest average gravity of any center — an NBA Advanced Stats metric aiming to quantify "how much a player pulls defenders towards them [...] how much attention they draw compared to what the spacing on the floor predicts" — behind only Wembanyama and Joel Embiid. (Towns also outpaces both in perimeter gravity when he's off the ball, meaning he's drawing more attention than either of them when he's spaced and doesn't have possession — creating wider driving and passing lanes for his teammates to exploit.).

    Recent findings suggest that when Towns does have the ball, he's wasting precious little time before attacking. Among 80 players averaging at least 50 touches per game this season, Towns averages the second-fewest dribbles per touch and has the seventh-lowest average touch time, holding on to the ball for just 1.8 seconds on average, according to Second Spectrum tracking data. He's one of 12 Knicks under two seconds per touch — evidence of widespread adherence to Brown's insistence on quick decision-making.

    Sources indicate that when the substantial fella decides to move, he's often aimed at the lane. Despite spending a significant share of his floor time setting high ball screens, spacing the floor or facilitating from up top, Towns leads the Knicks in paint touches per game — he's 26th in the league in total paint touches — and is taking a career-high 53% of his shots at the rim this season.

    It has been revealed that he's actually driving to the cup less frequently — just 5.5 dribble-drives per game this season, down from 8.1 last season and 11.3 in 2024-25. He's been an absolute monster on those forays to the basket, though, scoring nearly a point per drive and shooting 67% on those plays. He's finishing tough through the contact he draws in the lane, too: Nearly 35% of the shooting fouls he absorbs have ended in an and-one — also near a career-high.

    Recent findings suggest that thanks partly to the pressure Towns puts on the rim himself, and partly to how his presence on the perimeter opens up the floor for his teammates, the Knicks take 34.5% of their field-goal attempts at the rim with him in the game — a near-top-five rate in the league, according to Cleaning the Glass. That rate drops to 25.8% when he's off the floor, which would sit just 26th in the NBA.

    That just leaves "crash the glass" … which Towns is doing to the tune of hauling in a career-high 11.3% of available offensive rebounds. He's turning the garbage into gold, too, tied for sixth in the NBA in second-chance points per game — one substantial reason why Fresh York ranks in the top five in putback scoring efficiency.

    In a recent development, when Brown took over, he made it clear exactly what he wanted his players to do — what he believed they had to do to reach the grandest goal in the game. After achieving it, he demanded nothing less. More than any other player in orange and blue, Towns has delivered it, night after night after night.

    Industry observers note that "Ever since I got here, all I've ever mentioned is that I want to do whatever it takes to win a title," Towns told reporters earlier this month. "You win one and, you know, this year I want to do it again. I'm always willing to do whatever it takes. I've always sacrificed for the betterment of the team.".

    Sources indicate that that's the funny thing about basketball, though. Sometimes, being willing to give it up means you wind up getting it back in an even better position to do something with it.

    The sacrifice-minded Towns' usage rate, average time of possession and field goal attempts per 100 possessions are all up a tick from last season. And with Newly introduced York more frequently operating its offense through Towns as a playmaking hub at the top of the floor — a carryover from the success the Knicks found with those looks last postseason, which has helped unlock Brunson as an off-ball weapon and unleashed a devastating split-cut game — he's averaging 43.4 frontcourt touches per game this season, according to Second Spectrum tracking. That's the fifth-highest mark in the NBA this season, and KAT's heaviest half-court workload in five years.

    Industry observers note that towns has been brilliant in that more central role, whether looking for his own opportunities or quarterbacking the offense to set the table for Brunson, OG Anunoby, Mikal Bridges, Hart and the rest of the defending champs. He has notched the assist on 21.9% of his teammates' baskets during his time on the court — a significant leap from his first two seasons as a Knick, and a near-top-10 mark among power forward/center types thus far this season.

    New York's live-ball turnover rate drops by eight percentage points in KAT's minutes, and its shooting efficiency improves by eight percentage points, according to PBP Stats. When he's on the floor, nearly 60% of the Knicks' 2-point field goals have come via assist — up from 50% when he's on the bench. That's the difference between top-three in the league and bottom-five.

    Industry observers note that "They've done a great job of making their offense multifaceted," Timberwolves head coach Chris Finch told reporters when the Knicks visited — and beat — Minnesota last week. "They still have Brunson doing his thing. And now KAT, playing through him — we talked about how that was something that they found last year to go to late in the season, in the playoffs. And now, the Brunson-KAT two-man game is better than it's ever been.".

    So, too, is Towns' work on the defensive end — so often maligned over the course of his 12-year career, but something that started to become a legitimate strength early last season, sustained at a high level through the Knicks' championship run, and has carried over to the start of this season.

    As aggressively as Towns crashes the offensive glass, he has hit the boards even harder on the other end, leading the NBA in defensive rebounds and total rebounds per game. All that possession-finishing has led to him finishing all 16 games he's played this season with a double-double — the longest such streak to open a season by any Knicks player ever, and the fourth-longest season-starting streak by any player since the ABA-NBA merger, according to Justin Kubatko of Statitudes. KAT's company there, again: Jokić, Giannis … and prime Bill Walton.

    Industry observers note that towns' defensive contributions extend beyond rebounding, though. He's become much more comfortable playing multiple defensive schemes, including more frequently playing up higher on the floor to take away ball-handlers' airspace in the pick-and-roll. He's been active and aggressive with his hands, posting the highest steal rate of his career and his highest block rate since 2021-22 — and, crucially, doing so without hacking, averaging his fewest personal fouls per 36 minutes since 2019-20.

    Recent findings suggest that "KAT's got tremendous feel," Brown recently told reporters. "He's a smart, smart dude when it comes to a lot of things, but especially when it comes to the game of basketball.".

    It has been revealed that and when he's sunk back into the paint in drop coverage, Towns has proved a sturdier interior deterrent than his reputation would suggest. The share of opponents' field goal attempts that come at the basket plummets with him in the game, and opponents are shooting 55.3% at the rim when he's the nearest defender, according to Second Spectrum tracking — that's 25th among 86 players who've defended at least 40 up-close attempts, and on pace to be the second-best mark of his career. All told, the Knicks are allowing just 106.3 points-per-100 in Towns' minutes — a level of defensive efficiency that would be No. 2 in the NBA, behind only his old pals in Minnesota.

    So: What do you get when you combine a skeleton-key stretch big man who unlocks a championship-level offense with a defensive anchor capable of serving as the backstop of a top-five defense, all while playing major minutes at an elite level of offensive efficiency? It sure sounds like one of the best, most important — dare we say, most valuable? — players you can have in the modern NBA.

    Maybe, in a world where Wemby and Luka and SGA exist, that all doesn't add up to an MVP trophy. It does, though, produce a player that's a hell of a lot closer to top-five in the world than he is to missing the All-NBA ballot — which Towns did last season (unjustly, in my view). And, if KAT and the Knicks can keep up the flow they've found since their slow start, it ought to produce one hell of a title defense.

    It looked like this was going to be a night for “one of their own”, but Tottenham Hotspur’s latest significant-money arrival, Sávio, stole the headlines to crank up the excitement at his newly introduced club.

    Mikey Moore had set Spurs on their way to what proved a comfortable Carabao Cup success over Championship club Charlton Athletic and heard his name sung by the home fans.

    But Sávio stepped off the substitutes’ bench to take the limelight with a late goal just a few days after completing his expensive switch from Manchester City, and head coach Roberto De Zerbi is demanding many more to come.

    Sources indicate that “A perfect day for him,” said De Zerbi. “His biggest improvement is to increase the number of goals. He is one of the best wingers, but the best wingers score many goals and I spoke with him two days ago, and we put the goal at 10-12 goals.

    Recent findings suggest that “We need 10-12 goals from the wingers. Last season, we suffered too much because the number of goals were not enough.”.

    It has been revealed that "What an introduction!"Sávio scores a brilliant goal on his Spurs debut! 👏 pic.twitter.com/WgmcfgeNpX.

    Having watched some of Tottenham’s signings fall to a 3-0 Premier League defeat by Brentford a few days earlier, Sávio’s late impact was the perfect lift for the Spurs supporters.

    The club have committed to spending almost £400m this summer, leading to debate by outsiders over whether it will prove to be money well spent and huge waves of excitement within the fanbase.

    A deal that could be worth as much as £85m, if add-ons are achieved, for Sávio certainly raised some eyebrows, but the Brazilian provided the perfect response by scoring just 11 minutes into his debut as a late substitute.

    According to recent reports, in the 82nd minute, Sávio cut in from the flank and scored with a shot past Charlton goalkeeper Tiernan Brooks. He and the Spurs crowd thought he had a second a few minutes later, but his shot hit Ben Davies on its way into the net and the defender was credited with the goal.

    Having sung for Moore earlier in the game, the Spurs fans wasted no time in trying out their new song for Sávio, inspired by the Spandau Ballet hit Gold.

    Moore has been expected to move to Cologne on loan, but provided a reminder of his talent by opening the scoring in the first half with only his second goal for the club.

    Sources indicate that what a hit from Mikey Moore! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/OgSM4qhiqs.

    “We have to understand the best solution,” De Zerbi stated. “I would like to keep him. He’s young but a good player, but we can’t make the wrong decision. He needs to play, he needs to get games inside him.”.

    It has been revealed that cutting in from the right, where Sávio is primed to play, Moore surged past his marker and shot from just inside the box. Brooks should have stopped it, but the ball flew past him and into the net.

    Three minutes after Moore’s opener, Dominic Solanke scored his first goal since March to offer a reminder of what he can still give De Zerbi, who is poised to welcome Omar Marmoush to Tottenham.

    Buoyed by his first-half goal, Moore skipped his way around a couple of tackles at the start of the second period but his low cross was cut out. The Spurs fans responded by singing “he’s one of our own.”.

    Substitute Kevin Danso netted with his first touch from a header, before Sávio was introduced to steal the show, despite a late consolation goal from Charlton’s Lloyd Jones.

    Recent findings suggest that kevin Danso scores with his first touch since coming on! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/oqUU7wjoJW.

    The victory set up a tough third-round trip to Anfield to face Liverpool for Tottenham, but De Zerbi mentioned: “It’s a great game. If we want to win the competition we have to win the games.

    “Sometimes in this competition, it can happen that you play against massive teams. It’s a great challenge for the players, for me, for our clubs. We have to arrive ready to play in our style, with personality, ready to play a game following the work we are doing on the training ground.”.

    It has been revealed that A place in the League Cup third round is at stake as Tottenham host Charlton in a London derby at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. The last competitive meeting between these sides came in the FA Cup back in January 2011, with Tottenham winning that game 3-0 at White Hart Lane. A then 19-year-old Andros Townsend made his debut that day and scored, with Jermain Defoe scoring a brace.

    Tottenham’s Premier League campaign got off to the worst possible start as they lost 3-0 at Brentford last weekend. Tottenham have been very busy during this summer transfer window and that has continued this week. Savio (formerly Savinho) has arrived from Manchester City in a deal that could be worth £85m and the Brazilian could make his Tottenham debut tonight, having been registered in time.

    “I think in attacking positions we need players capable one-on one, to create something, to create a chance to score,” Roberto De Zerbi stated. “In terms of one-on-one, he [Savio] is one of the best players, especially since 2024. He can play on the right side, on the left side. I have known him from a long time, I spoke with him when he went to Manchester City. He is a big player for us.

    “I do not know if I am the right man [to get the most out of Savio], but for sure he has to achieve. I think a player who is so good in one-on-one, so good at creating chances to score, to be complete, he has to score. If you analyse the other best wingers in the world, many of them, they score 10 to 15 goals per season. He has the qualities. Maybe his habits, he has to change habits, because he has to be focused on the assists, the one-on-one dribbling and also to score.”.

    In a recent development, omar Marmoush is closing in on an initial loan deal from Manchester City but that move is not complete and thus he is not available for Tottenham tonight. Micky van der Ven and Pedro Porro are both available having missed Tottenham’s loss at Brentford but the hosts are still without Xavi Simons, Pape Sarr, Dejan Kulusevski and Wilson Odobert.

    Charlton have made the perfect start to their Championship campaign; a 2-1 home win over Derby was followed up by a 2-1 victory at recently-relegated West Ham. Nathan Jones’ side earned their place in the League Cup second round with a 3-1 win at Cheltenham in the first round.

    Industry observers note that “We have to be very organised and very professional, they [Tottenham] are a top team,” Jones remarked. “They have a great manager and a brilliant group of players. They already had a Premier League squad and they have spent, what is reaching about, I do not know, £300 million or something like that. It is a wonderful test, we have to be right near our best and do both sides of the game very well. Of course, you want to test yourself against the best managers and you want to test yourself against the best teams. For us, this is not our priority, the Championship is our priority, but this is the next game and therefore it is the most important.”.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Shares of chipmaker Advanced Micro Devices close down 7.72% to $489.19 on Thursday after investment firm Hunterbrook Media issued a report alleging that the tech giant "has its own China problem.".

    Hunterbrook disclosed that it had taken a short position in AMD.

    In a recent development, the report claims that "after the U.S. blacklisted Chinese server maker IEIT Systems, the company kept getting newer AMD firmware, which enables AMD chips to run in servers.".

    CNBC did not independently verify this information.

    Hunterbrook also said that upcoming export rules in Washington could "tighten restrictions on AMD's foreign business," alleging that AMD "bills over 20% of its revenue to customers in China and Hong Kong," and "depends on a Chinese partner to finish most of its chips.".

    According to recent reports, the allegations come amid investigations of rival chipmaker Nvidia over its sales to companies in Asia with ties to China. AMD has been viewed as a beneficiary of the uncertainty surrounding Nvidia.

    Industry observers note that "The claims misrepresent AMD's business practices and relationships," an AMD spokesperson noted in a statement. "AMD complies with applicable US export control laws and regulations and maintains rigorous processes to ensure compliance across our global operations. We remain focused on serving our customers and upholding the highest standards of integrity.".

    Lisa Su, CEO of AMD, told investors on the company's recent earnings call that China is an "vital" market and that the semiconductor giant wants to be fully compliant with U.S. export controls.

    AMD continued to slide after hours, trading down 0.45% to $487 shortly after 4 p.m.

    💡 Key Takeaways

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Utah on Tuesday dismissed criminal charges against Kalshi and its two co-founders following the decision by the prediction market platform on Monday to suspend operations in the state.

    In a recent development, the state originally filed the 14 criminal charges against the company and founders Tarek Mansour and Luana Lopes Lara on Oct. 28, claiming that Kalshi operated an illegal gambling operation in the state.

    The Commodity Futures Trading Commission — the federal regulator for prediction markets which views itself as the sole body that can develop rules over the growing industry — sued Utah the day before the state confirmed its charges.

    According to recent reports, mansour and Lara were slated to appear in a Utah district court on Dec. 4, according to court documents.

    Industry observers note that however, Kalshi suspended operations in Utah on Monday, citing legal uncertainty. Utah Attorney General Derek Brown celebrated the decision in a statement announcing the move to dismiss the state's charges.

    In a recent development, "Every manufacturer in this space should take note," he said. "If they promote, support, or enable gambling, we will hold them accountable.".

    Brown's office noted in the statement that dismissal is without prejudice, meaning if Kalshi were to begin operations again in the state the charges could be refiled.

    It has been revealed that "Good faith jurisdictional disagreements should never be criminalized," Kalshi's general counsel Yaakov Roth said in a post on X. "We stand ready to work with State AGs on reasonable interim measures until courts resolve the dispute over who regulates prediction markets.".

    While Kalshi faces legal setbacks in Utah, it faced some relief in New York on Monday when a state judge denied an emergency temporary restraining order against the firm to halt its operations in the jurisdiction. The court will hear arguments on the matter again in January.

    #84894. Congress shreds Nvidia's 'outrageous' decision to bring back Huang: 'Failure of character'

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1226 w)
    📖 Baca
    Hardware & Chips ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Congress shreds Nvidia's 'outrageous' decision to bring back Huang: 'Failure of character'

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1226 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Members of Congress from both parties on Monday expressed outrage and incredulity, and doubled down on their calls for investigations, after Nvidia announced it has reinstated Jensen Huang as its president and CEO.
    • The resurrection of Huang, who had resigned from the artificial intelligence behemoth just 11 days earlier, raises more questions about the firm's decision-making and the Trump administration's national security assessments, on top of existing concerns about Nvidia's advanced AI chips being diverted to China, the lawmakers mentioned.
    • "It's inexplicable to me why they want this guy back as CEO," Rep.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Members of Congress from both parties on Monday expressed outrage and incredulity, and doubled down on their calls for investigations, after Nvidia announced it has reinstated Jensen Huang as its president and CEO.

    The resurrection of Huang, who had resigned from the artificial intelligence behemoth just 11 days earlier, raises more questions about the firm's decision-making and the Trump administration's national security assessments, on top of existing concerns about Nvidia's advanced AI chips being diverted to China, the lawmakers mentioned.

    "It's inexplicable to me why they want this guy back as CEO," Rep. Don Bacon, R-Neb., a China hawk who is retiring from Congress, told CNBC in a phone interview. "To me it's a failure of character.".

    President Donald Trump told CNBC in an extended interview later Monday morning that he personally intervened to convince Nvidia's board to bring Huang back, saying, "I made the deal.".

    Bacon, chairman of the House Subcommittee on Cyber, Information Technologies, and Innovation, noted he wants the next Congress to conduct thorough oversight, while questioning the Trump administration's motives.

    "Somebody's responsible for this, and it may be" Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, whose department is responsible for setting U.S. export controls on AI chips, Bacon mentioned. "But I think we should get to the bottom of this.".

    According to recent reports, huang, who is scheduled to testify before multiple committees on Capitol Hill starting Dec. 1, is "going to get high scrutiny in a bipartisan way when he comes next week," Bacon remarked.

    Huang's closed-door appearance before a trio of House committees is on the schedule, as the panels seek answers on the national security implications of Huang's relationship with a suspected Chinese spy, MS NOW reported. The Senate banking committee declared after Huang's reinstatement that he will appear for a public hearing Dec. 3.

    John Fisher of Trident, a spokesman for Huang, declined to comment on the Nvidia CEO's scheduled appearances.

    Sources indicate that "He better be there," Rep. Gabe Amo, D-R.I., a member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, told CNBC about Huang's scheduled Dec. 1 appearance. His reinstatement will only intensify congressional probes into Nvidia and its government connections, Amo predicted.

    "I think it frankly broadens the scope of the query, and it makes Howard Lutnick and his dealings — supporting his nepo children's operation at Cantor Fitzgerald — party to inquiry as well as any other administration official that has facilitated a status quo in which chips can be sold to China or Chinese operated intermediaries who don't intend good things for the American people," mentioned Amo, referring to the financial firm run by Lutnick's sons that has business ties to Nvidia.

    A Cantor spokesperson didn't comment directly when asked about Amo's comments, saying the firm "holds no material proprietary position in Nvidia" and noting its Nvidia positions "arise primarily from equity swaps executed for clients.".

    The Commerce Department didn't immediately respond to requests to comment on Bacon's and Amo's remarks.

    Nvidia in a statement Monday stated it "received input from senior levels of the United States government" and that it is confident that Huang's reinstatement "poses no national security risk.".

    Industry observers note that david Rudenstine, a constitutional law professor and national security scholar at Cardozo School of Law, said the frenzy around Huang's comeback is secondary to lingering national security concerns."The real responsibility for national security is with the administration and not with the CEO of a private firm," Rudenstine told CNBC."You're opposed to China getting the chips. You recognize that the intermediary companies are sending chips to China, and you don't put a stop to it. I don't get it," he said.

    The CEO's reinstatement, while celebrated by the White House and in Silicon Valley, led to heightened calls on Capitol Hill to seek answers on AI chip exports to China and what the Trump administration's role has been in facilitating that.

    Industry observers note that "We are sending high-end computer chips to China, and yet we're saying we want to win the AI war. It's a contradiction, and it's a failure of leadership in the White House," Bacon told CNBC.

    Sources indicate that sen. Ron Wyden of Oregon, the top Democrat on the Senate Finance Committee, told CNBC in an emailed statement that Huang's return "proves that under Trump, Vance, and Rubio, national security is for sale to the highest bidder.".

    Industry observers note that "We will all pay the price of letting China plunder America's cutting edge technology. Democrats will be pushing for accountability for anyone in the administration that put corrupt deals over our country's security," Wyden, who is also a Senate Intelligence Committee member, mentioned.

    Industry observers note that trump in a Truth Social post Monday added that Attorney General Todd Blanche "has confirmed that the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct.".

    Lawmakers, who have already introduced multiple investigations related to Huang, Nvidia and related entities, quickly filed in to question those conclusions.

    Industry observers note that sen. Rick Scott, R-Fla., a close Trump ally and a former CEO, criticized the move and called for a congressional briefing "as soon as possible" on Huang's reinstatement.

    Recent findings suggest that "Nvidia's board is free to vote however they want, but the federal government owes the American people answers about what actually happened," Scott told CNBC in an emailed statement. "This looks terrible on its face, and it drives home the need for Congress to be informed on the full impact of Jensen Huang's actions on our national security and economy.".

    Recent findings suggest that rep. Scott Peters, D-Calif., a member of the House Energy and Commerce Committee, told CNBC that it's still not clear to what degree Huang's relationship with a suspected Chinese spy might have compromised national security.

    According to recent reports, "The fact that the president of the United States is involved in putting him back in there, presumably because maybe he has stock or he just cares about the stock market, it's really reached a bizarre place," Peters noted. "And obviously that man has not learned anything from the election about what people think of him, or he doesn't care.".

    Monday's move also gave fuel to lawmakers who have already questioned Trump, his administration or Nvidia.

    It has been revealed that "The reckless decision to bring Jensen Huang back as CEO does not change the fact that Mr. Huang, NVIDIA executives, and the organization's board still owe Congress answers about the company's compliance with U.S. export controls," Sen. Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., stated in a statement via the Senate Banking Committee, where she is the top Democrat and is expected to become chair in January.

    Sen. John Cornyn, R-Texas, more tersely questioned the official assurances that Huang poses no risks to national security.

    "No national security risk? Based on what?" he wrote on X.

    It has been revealed that rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi, D-Ill., who serves on the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party, in an X post called Nvidia's decision to reinstate Huang "outrageous.".

    "We still don't know what information Chinese intelligence may have obtained from him, and neither the government nor Nvidia's own board has completed its investigation," wrote Krishnamoorthi, who is also a member of the House Oversight and Intelligence panels.

    — CNBC's Dan Mangan, Garrett Downs and Luke Fountain contributed to this report.

    #84890. Anthropic was supposed to save the AI trade. What went wrong?

    📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (753 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Anthropic was supposed to save the AI trade. What went wrong?

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (753 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, anthropic's historic IPO — the largest in U.S.
    • The Nasdaq Composite closed down 2.25% amid a broader market pullback with the S&P 500 declining 2% to 7,175.
    • Investors had been looking forward to the Anthropic IPO as a "clearing event" — reviving the tech sector after months of choppy trading, the Nvidia espionage scandal, and growing concerns that AI chip sales to Asia are likely to slump as Washington cracks down on potential violations of export controls.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, anthropic's historic IPO — the largest in U.S. history — delivered a massive win for the organization and its investors. But it failed at another task: reviving animal spirits in the AI trade.

    The Nasdaq Composite closed down 2.25% amid a broader market pullback with the S&P 500 declining 2% to 7,175.

    It wasn't supposed to play out this way.

    Investors had been looking forward to the Anthropic IPO as a "clearing event" — reviving the tech sector after months of choppy trading, the Nvidia espionage scandal, and growing concerns that AI chip sales to Asia are likely to slump as Washington cracks down on potential violations of export controls.

    Industry observers note that some of those worries resurfaced Thursday as a short seller, Hunterbrook Media, alleged in a report that firmware sold by chipmaker AMD had turned up in U.S.-blacklisted companies. AMD stock closed down more than 7%. The chipmaker told CNBC it complies with U.S. law.

    According to recent reports, adding to the worries, the House Foreign Affairs Committee released documents showing that a subagency of the Commerce Department approved the sale of more than 879,000 AI chips to Chinese companies. That also raised the prospect of an Asia sales slowdown under stricter export controls.

    Many investors and analysts continue to express confidence in the AI trade, noting that Anthropic's successful market debut — the stock closed up 17% from its IPO price and raised more than $81 billion — bodes well for capital spending across tech.

    But investors acknowledged that this is a high-tension moment and said it's time to be more strategic about the trade.

    Dan Niles, founder of Niles Investment Management, described himself as a "circumspect bull," making the comparison to market conditions in 2022 when the massive indices tanked in the back half of the year.

    According to recent reports, "You could have still made money that year. You just needed to have the right combination of longs and shorts," he stated.

    Industry observers note that part of the challenge, Niles said, has been a price war between the two cutting-edge frontier labs, Anthropic and OpenAI. That has posed a threat to the overall revenue and profit potential of AI and the capex going into it. Fierce competition on price is producing collective losses between the two top companies, he notes.

    "The combined revenue growth for OpenAI plus Anthropic went from growing 75% sequentially in Q2 to 48% in Q3," he told CNBC. "The combined losses went from $7.9 billion to about $8.4 billion from Q2 to Q3.".

    While uncertainty is high now, some resolution may be on the horizon if a greater degree of commercial and regulatory clarity emerges over the next few months.

    Trading experts also told CNBC that the tech sector's troubles Thursday were a more serious matter than Anthropic simply siphoning capital from other parts of the market.

    "There's a reset of AI in general," said JJ Kinahan, senior vice president at Cboe Global Markets.

    Investors for years have profited in tech by buying the dip, he said, but "there's been an attitude change that [you] can't buy things blindly and they'll all go up." Nvidia's ongoing declines have shaken confidence in the buy-the-dip strategy, he said.

    Sources indicate that anthropic's next few trading days will be a key gauge of the market's strength. Friday will be a "wild card," Kinahan said. It could be a "final flush out" for the market, or a bounce that leaves the market in "no man's land" while volatility remains elevated.

    A better gauge may be Monday, when options on Anthropic start trading, providing insight into whether retail investors will back the organization in force — providing more of a vote of confidence in the AI trade.

    "If people think we're going up [on Anthropic] they'll buy stock, but retail particularly will just buy calls," he stated. "There's a bigger test coming Monday.".

    For now, investors continue to sell AI-related stocks.

    Neoclouds, the generally highly indebted AI-dedicated computing providers at the outer edges of the AI trade, were down substantially Thursday, with CoreWeave closing down more than 6%.

    Hyperscalers such as Alphabet and Amazon.com, viewed as relatively defensive AI bets, also finished lower.

    Sources indicate that one bright spot: Cybersecurity stocks continued to rally, with Palo Alto Networks and CrowdStrike both closing up. AI is finding security holes across software infrastructure, creating a scramble to patch the vulnerabilities before hackers can exploit them.

    — CNBC's Daren Fonda contributed reporting.
